reframing_when: The question treats a human-chosen boundary as an immutable wall when that constraint could be relaxed, removed, or redefined — the frame/lens is being mistaken for reality.
The question has no explicit constraints and is therefore too vague to produce actionable answers — adding the right boundary would sharpen the inquiry.
The question includes constraints that were inherited from a prior context but no longer apply — organizational or technical boundaries have shifted but the question hasn't.
The question asks 'how do we do everything?' when the real question is 'what should we cut?' — the absence of a don't-do constraint leads to boiling the ocean.
reframing_move: Test the walls: ask 'which of these constraints are real (physics, law, budget) and which are assumed (organizational habit, precedent, fear)?' — then reframe the question with only the real constraints, opening the space that the assumed ones were closing.
curation_note: Constraints operates on question structure by distinguishing real boundaries from assumed ones. The source is explicit: constraints can be 'helpful, even inspiring' when they are the right constraints, and dangerous when inherited from a prior context. The Cukier framing research (RFC) independently identifies 'mutable constraints treated as walls' as a core frame pattern — this model provides the reframing lens.

reframing_when.note: All four activations grounded: wall vs door (creative catalyst analogy), missing constraints causing vagueness (TOSCA framework), inherited constraints (boundaries of analysis example), and absence of don't-do list (boil the ocean anti-pattern).

frame_patterns_challenged.note: Scope lock: the question's boundaries may be assumed, not real. Option space collapse: testing constraints opens alternatives the question's frame was hiding.
